messages:
ana: Hey folks — noticed a weird degradation on the atlas-13k quant bring-up. Long prompts with a trailing instructional suffix get increasingly short, off-topic tails after ~9k tokens. Looks like the KV tail is being trimmed earlier than our window policy. :thinking:

mike: Can you repro locally? model name + quant config?

ana: (typo) ana: repro on ci/gpu-6, `atlas-13k-int4v2`, `quant-backend=v2`, conv-mode=dynamic-tiling. Happens only when we include a long generated system note + many short user messages appended.

leah: Hmm. I ran a quick run with `--kv-inspect` and saw the tail index jump back by ~2048 mid-generation. Grepping the logs gave: 
```
[2026-02-28T14:03:12Z] kv_reindex: tail_idx 24576 -> 22528 (evict_len=2048)
[2026-02-28T14:03:12Z] kv_window: effective_window=12288, configured=16384
```
No explicit eviction call in the same trace.

mike: That effective_window drop is suspicious. Could be tiling logic miscomputing stride when sequence distribution has many short segments. Any reproducer?

ana: Minimal repro attached below (python). It's tiny:
```python
# repro.py
from client import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(model='atlas-13k-int4v2')
ctx = 'SYSTEM:\n' + 'A'*9000 + '\n'
for i in range(80):
    ctx += f'user{i}: short question?\\n'
resp = rc.generate(ctx, max_tokens=512, kv_inspect=True)
print(resp.text)
```

leah: Ran that and got a drifted answer after token ~9200. KV dump showed a missing contiguous block in the middle of the tail. Dump snippet: 
```
KV_DUMP idx: 22000..22499 -> present
KV_DUMP idx: 22500..22799 -> MISSING
KV_DUMP idx: 22800..24500 -> present
```
That gap is exactly one `tiling_stride` (2048) and aligns with the `evict_len` above.

derek: Could be a race between dynamic-tiling compaction and quant buffer GC. We changed the compaction watermark last week (PR #6789). @mike can you run bisect with old compaction?

mike: On it. Mirroring environment now. If it's the PR, we should see the gap go away with the previous compaction heuristic. Running: `./tools/ci_bisect.sh --pr-rev=origin/main~1 --run=repro.py`

perf-bot: ci run queued on gpu-6 (job 4421). ETA ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ana: Also, note this only shows when `quant-backend=v2` and dynamic-tiling active. With `quant-backend=v1` or `tiling=static` the window stays full and no gap.

leah: One more odd detail — RoPE embeddings seem to rescale across the gap boundary. The rotated indices before gap and after gap have a small phase offset; might explain coherence drop.

mike: If RoPE rescaling is drifting, it could be an indexing mismatch when stitching shards after compaction. I'll add extra checks to the stitcher to assert contiguous index monotonicity.

derek: Also add a diagnostic that dumps `kv_index_map` at compaction boundaries. If we can capture a postmortem we'll know whether it's a bookkeeping bug vs intentional early trim.

ana: Thanks. For now tagging this as high-impact for the bring-up: long-context QA fails at ~9k with this config. I'll drop the failing traces and KV dumps in the thread artifact bucket: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/atlas-13k/3301112223/

leah: Upload done. Link: https://s3.redwood/example/atlas-13k/3301112223/kv-dump.tar.gz :mag_right:

mike: Bisect result: PR #6789 appears correlated. Rolling compaction heuristic back removed the gap on my repro. Next steps: add index monotonicity asserts + guard in compaction + small unit test.

ana: Great. If fixes are small we should consider a hotfix to the dedicated pools before wider rollouts. This is probably going to hurt long-context customers. :eyes:

derek: Agreed. I'll prepare a patch and a canary build. If anyone wants to pair on the asserts ping me.

leah: I'll run extended fuzz against tiling + int4v2 overnight with the new assert.

ana: Thanks all — will update after the canary. :thumbsup:
